item.title: The Origins of Valentine's Day: A Surprisingly Dark Roman Tradition
item.description: The origins of Valentine’s Day stretch back long before heart shaped chocolates and red roses filled store shelves. The history behind Valentine’s Day includes dark origins, muddled stories and a surprising amount of chance.

item.description: Koalas are iconic Australian animals, but people often pause when asked, "What is a group of koalas called?" The short answer is that there is no widely accepted official collective noun for koalas.

item.description: The pluralist democracy model explains how power spreads across many groups rather than resting in one place.

item.title: The Arctic Food Web (and Why Ice Matters So Much)
item.description: The arctic food web explains how energy moves through one of the coldest ecosystems on Earth. From microscopic algae trapped in sea ice to apex predators like polar bears, every organism depends on another for food.

item.title: 10 Prayers for Anxiety to Help You Summon Calm
item.description: In difficult moments, many people turn to prayer to quiet an anxious heart. Prayers for anxiety offer a way to lay down worries, seek wisdom, and find peace in the midst of stress.

item.title: What Is a Group of Hawks Called? It's About the Shape They Take in Flight
item.description: People often wonder, "What is a group of hawks called," when they see many birds circling high in the sky. Hawks are generally solitary birds, so the answer depends on context rather than a single catchall word.

item.title: What Is a Group of Polar Bears Called? Sounds Sneaky
item.description: If you have ever wondered, "What is a group of polar bears called," you are not alone. The short answer: A group of polar bears is called a sleuth. Yes, sleuth—like a detective on the ice.

item.title: The 10 Highest-Valued Companies Aren't All What You Think
item.description: The highest-valued companies dominate headlines because their market cap towers over competitors. Market capitalization measures a company’s market value by multiplying its current share price by the number of outstanding shares, giving investors a snapshot of market value.
